title: People
text:
Current team members

Emmanuel Owusu Ahenkan (SACEMA)      













Emmanuel Owusu Ahenkan is a PhD student at the South African Centre for Epidemiological Modelling and Analysis (SACEMA), Stellenbosch University. He holds a Master of Science degree in Mathematical Sciences and another in Machine Learning. He is passionate about applying mathematical modelling and artificial intelligence techniques to address health challenges in Africa. His research in this project focuses on modelling the impact of incorporating wastewater surveillance as a routine method for influenza control.




Kath O’Reilly (LSHTM)    













Kathleen O’Reilly is an Associate Professor in statistics for infectious diseases at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine. Dr O’Reilly is the co-Director of the internationally recognised Centre for Mathematical Modelling of Infectious Diseases (LSHTM). Her research interests are in the use of data analytics to prevent outbreaks and solve challenges in epidemiology. The research team at LSHTM are modelling partners for Unicef in the Global Polio Eradication Initiative, where analysis and modelling are used to support polio eradication challenges and inform policy. Activities in environmental and wastewater surveillance have stemmed from its use in polio eradication, and during the COVID-19 pandemic several projects were established to better understand SARS-CoV-2 spread from wastewater. In the METSI-PH consortia Kath is supporting the research of several group members, including PhD and MSc supervision. Additionally, Kath will develop research in how vale of information methods can be used to evaluate wastewater data.

Mukhlid Yousif (NICD)  





Dr Mukhlid Yousif is a Researcher, and Senior Genomics and Public Health Scientist with over 15 years of experience in molecular virology, bioinformatics, and genomic epidemiology. His research spans hepatitis B virus, HIV drug resistance, measles, rubella, and polio. He co-established the Wastewater Genomics Syndicate at the National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD) in South Africa, leading the development and implementation of multi-pathogen wastewater surveillance to inform public health responses. Dr Yousif has led international collaborations and consortia, received multiple grants, published over 20 peer-reviewed articles, supervised postgraduate students, and works closely with regional and global partners to strengthen diseases surveillance using wastewater across Africa.
